title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $4.56: median sales 157 (75.6% of baseline); noise-adjusted estimate from past price hikes supports ~24% drop.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short warning
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk; may lead to out-of-stocks, reducing actual sales even if demand is stable.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is a known demand reducer. Past price hikes to $4.56 (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 195 and 119—median 157, or 75.6% of baseline. This suggests a ~24% demand reduction. The supplier's delivery short warning adds supply-side risk, lowering available units, but demand may still drop if customers see out-of-stocks. No event or promotion is scheduled. The uplift model suggests no effect, but price and supply risk are real drivers. Shrink effect toward 1.0 due to limited data on this exact price point. Confidence is medium.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.2 - 290.7 | 10%-90%: 156.0 - 281.5

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
